text:
GitHub stopped treating AI agents like a feature and started treating them like staff.

Agent HQ is live, and Agent Plugins 1.0 shipped this month for VS Code, the Copilot CLI, and the Copilot app. What that actually means: you can assign coding agents from different vendors inside GitHub itself, watch them work side by side, and compare what they hand back.

Underneath it, the Copilot coding agent takes a real issue, works asynchronously in a sandboxed Actions environment, and opens a draft pull request for review.

That is the whole shift. You stop typing prompts and start assigning work. The review stays human.

We build this entire content engine that way. Nothing here publishes until a person merges the PR.

Try it this week: pick one small, boring issue in a repo you own. Assign it. Review the draft PR like you would a teammate's.

text:
There are four levels of AI. Most people stop at level two and think they've arrived.

We drew this out live on Tech Thursday, so here it is properly.

Level 1 is the model. The raw engine. You don't live here, you rent it.

Level 2 is the chat. You type into a box and read the answer back. This is the consumer level, and it's where almost everyone stays.

Level 3 is the workflow. Scheduling, automations, a repeating path. A lot of people call this an agent. It isn't. It's a loop, and loops are still valuable.

Level 4 is the build. You direct the work inside the repo itself, with a CLI as your build partner, and you ship something that didn't exist.

The move isn't jumping to four. It's climbing one level this week. Take the task you repeat most often and build it instead of prompting it.

Save this and find your level.
